text:
Alex: Quick follow-up from the GQA/MQA kernel selection RFC — ran a short canary and hit a weird muxing case where grouped-query lanes started rejecting small single-query requests under KV-warm conditions. Not sure if this is a heuristics bug or an interface mismatch.
Maria: Can you paste the failing request shape? seq lenses, batch size, model variant?
Alex: Sure — most were seq_len 64-128, a mix of single-query and 8x small queries bundled. Model = rw-instruct-v1, kernel candidates = [mqa-grouped, gqa-default]. Observed: single-query request routed to grouped lane, then queued ~120ms, while gqa would have returned ~30ms.
Ryan: That smells like our lane scoring: we compute cost_est = base_cost * seq_ratio + batch_penalty. If the batch estimator overweights prefix reuse we may prefer grouped. Did you enable the "prefer_cache_hits" flag?
Alex: Yes, prefer_cache_hits=true in the canary config. Disabling it made the router prefer gqa again.
Sneha: If prefer_cache_hits flips routing aggressively, we need a fallthrough cap otherwise small tail latency suffers. We saw similar tail spikes in the last A/B.
Jordan: Strong +1 for a fallthrough cap. Also consider a cheap sanity check: if estimated_latency(grouped) > p99(gqa) * 1.5 then prefer gqa. Keeps grouped for throughput but avoids tail regressions.
Maria: How stable is p99(gqa) in the region? If it's noisy the check could flip a lot. We should use a smoothed p99 (exponential) and a minimum sample window.
Ryan: Implementation note: the router lives in rust-runner; adding another signal is cheap, but we need to propagate the smoothed metric into the routing decision API. Current call: select_kernel(request_meta, lane_stats) -> kernel_id. We can add optional heuristics: select_kernel(request_meta, lane_stats, runtime_flags).
Alex: Proposal: add two small changes: 1) route_debug reasons tagged on every selection (list of strings) so we can trace why grouped was chosen; 2) a soft-fallback cap config: max_expected_latency_ratio (default 2.0) and smoothing window = 5m.
Sneha: +1. Also add a backpressure token so grouped won't accept new singletons when queue_depth > lane_capacity * 0.8. That avoids head-of-line blocking.
Jordan: For the SDK/console UI, surface the reason codes as "kernel_choice_reason" in the trace logs — devs will appreciate clarity.
Maria: We should add a small experiment matrix: (A) current config, (B) prefer_cache_hits=false, (C) prefer_cache_hits=true + max_expected_latency_ratio=1.5 + backpressure. Measure p50/p95/p99 latency for singletons and batched flows and throughput.
Alex: I ran a quick run: (A) singleton p50=28ms p99=220ms, batched throughput=1200 tok/s; (B) singleton p50=32ms p99=95ms, batched throughput=900 tok/s; (C) singleton p50=30ms p99=80ms, batched throughput=1100 tok/s. Numbers are noisy but suggest the cap helps.
Ryan: Those are promising. Can you share the exact router config snippet?
Alex: Paste: ```json
{
  "prefer_cache_hits": true,
  "max_expected_latency_ratio": 1.5,
  "backpressure_threshold": 0.8,
  "smoothing_window_sec": 300
}
```
Maria: Two quick tradeoffs to call out in the follow-up RFC: (1) additional metrics surface cost and complexity in the control plane; (2) default conservative settings may reduce peak throughput for tail improvements. We need to document these clearly.
Sneha: Also add a migration plan: default-off flags, opt-in canary, then enable for high-load clusters only. Users on Dedicated might want different defaults.
Jordan: For Private deployments we should make the smoothing window configurable by ops teams — their telemetry cadence differs.
InfraBot: deploy-bot: canary rollout for router-config "gqa-mqa-mux-v2" started to 5% clusters at 2024-04-09T15:07:40Z :rocket:
Alex: Action items: (1) Ryan to add route_debug reasons and the new API arg (PR by end of week). (2) Maria to draft RFC addendum documenting heuristics + migration. (3) Sneha to design the backpressure gate and test harness. (4) Jordan to add console trace field. I'll run wider canary with config C once PR lands.
Ryan: I'll send a quick PR and include unit tests for the latency check.
Maria: I'll include experiment matrix and recommended defaults.
Sneha: I'll build the harness — want to capture both cold and KV-warm paths.
Jordan: lgtm. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Alex: Thanks — leaning toward enabling cap-by-default for hosted canaries after we validate. We'll reconvene next Tue if anything surprising pops up.
